Copilot CLI: approve once. Keep the boundary.

The October 21 update lets subagents honor custom and MCP tool approvals without duplicate permission prompts. Inherited approval is not unlimited access.

Try this week: in a test folder, approve one narrowly scoped tool, delegate one task, then inspect the output. Less interruption. The same responsibility.

Copilot CLI v1.0.104 changed when Autopilot stops waiting.

What changed: the October 27 release keeps interactive and SDK Autopilot sessions waiting for attached background tasks instead of stopping at COPILOT_TASK_WAIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS. Prompt-mode runs using -p --autopilot still honor that timeout.

What it does: the parent session keeps waiting for attached work. That is not proof the task succeeded, and it is not a promise that work survives a closed session.

Builder value: an image batch, build, or test run needs a clear finish line, not just a confident reply. In the latest Tech Thursday, Copilot CLI connected through MCP to generate a batch of images; the host then inspected them and found the quality wasn't right. Completion and acceptance are different checks.

Try this week: in an interactive test session, ask for a background task that writes output/draft.md. Define the expected contents first. Wait for the task result, open the actual file, and compare it with your brief. For scripted -p runs, test the timeout behavior separately.

The signal: AI work is moving beyond a single response. Builders need to track what is running, what arrived, and what passed review. Keep human approval before anything publishes.

Save this for your next agent workflow.
